Consider the following C code. Assume that unsigned long int type length is 64 bits.

The value returned when we call fun with the input $2^{40}$ is
explanation:
Step 1: Analyze the first loop.
The first loop is for (i = n; i > 1; i = i/2) j++;.
Given $n = 2^{40}$, the value of $i$ starts at $2^{40}$ and is halved in each iteration until $i = 1$.
The loop executes $40$ times, so after this loop finishes, $j = 40$.

Step 2: Analyze the second loop.
The second loop is for ( ; j > 1; j = j/2) sum++; with initial $j = 40$ and $sum = 0$.
Tracing the execution step-by-step:
• Iteration 1: $j = 40 > 1$, $sum$ becomes $1$, $j$ updates to $\lfloor 40/2 \rfloor = 20$.
• Iteration 2: $j = 20 > 1$, $sum$ becomes $2$, $j$ updates to $\lfloor 20/2 \rfloor = 10$.
• Iteration 3: $j = 10 > 1$, $sum$ becomes $3$, $j$ updates to $\lfloor 10/2 \rfloor = 5$.
• Iteration 4: $j = 5 > 1$, $sum$ becomes $4$, $j$ updates to $\lfloor 5/2 \rfloor = 2$.
• Iteration 5: $j = 2 > 1$, $sum$ becomes $5$, $j$ updates to $\lfloor 2/2 \rfloor = 1$.
• Loop condition check: $j = 1 > 1$ evaluates to false, so the loop terminates.

Step 3: Conclusion.
The function returns $sum = 5$. Hence, option (B) is the correct answer.
